conventions.correlation: Pearson correlation. Complete-case uses the same all-five rows for every entry; pairwise uses every jointly observed row separately for each entry.
conventions.higham: Unweighted Higham alternating PSD/unit-diagonal projections with Dykstra correction; convergence tolerance 1e-14.
conventions.rebonato_jackel: Clip correlation eigenvalues below zero, then rescale the spectral root to restore a unit diagonal.
conventions.standard_deviation: Sample standard deviation (ddof=1) from each series' full available history.

reconcile.dominant_decision_explanation: The complete-case/pairwise gap is far larger than either repair distance, so estimator choice matters more here than the choice between the two repairs.
reconcile.negative_variance_explanation: The pairwise matrix has a negative eigenvalue, so it is not PSD: there exists a weight vector with w' Sigma w < 0. The tracking position is close to that inconsistent direction and produces the reported negative variance.
reconcile.repair_uses: Matrix geometry and equal Frobenius cost per entry, not the number of observations behind each correlation.

conventions.demeaning: Subtract the ordinary full-sample arithmetic-return mean before every subsequent calculation.
conventions.ew_variance: Finite-sample normalized weights proportional to lambda^lag, newest observation highest; sum(w*r^2), with no weighted recentering and no Bessel correction because returns were already demeaned as instructed.
conventions.historical_quantile: Course RiskStats.jl convention: sort n values, set ndn=floor(n*alpha), nup=ceil(n*alpha) in one-based indexing, and average those two order statistics 50/50.
conventions.normal_var: Positive loss = -Phi^{-1}(0.05) * sigma * $1,000,000; demeaned return mean is zero.
conventions.sample_variance_and_moments: Variance/standard deviation use ddof=1; skewness and excess kurtosis use finite-sample bias corrections.
conventions.student_t: Three-parameter maximum likelihood fit (df, location, scale) to demeaned returns; scale is not the standard deviation.

ew_noise_comparison.conclusion: The VaR gap is not convincingly larger than estimation noise: it is below one lambda=0.94 standard error and below the conservative root-sum-square scale.

prediction.reason: The last roughly 40 days are much more volatile. EW(0.94) should react most, followed by EW(0.97). Before fitting, the full-sample heavy tails suggest Student-t above historical and both above equal-weight Normal at the 5% tail.

reconcile.kurtosis_explanation: Each 40/460-day regime is close to Normal in kurtosis, while mixing their very different variances creates large full-sample excess kurtosis. The fitted t is mainly a one-distribution approximation to this volatility-regime mixture.
reconcile.opinion_capital: Opinion: use lambda=0.97 for a capital number because its larger effective sample size produces a more stable estimate, while still assigning most weight to the new regime.
reconcile.opinion_trading_limit: Opinion: use lambda=0.94 for a trading limit because quicker adaptation to the active high-volatility regime is worth the additional estimator noise.
reconcile.ranking_surprise: Student-t MLE is the smallest 5% VaR, contrary to the initial ranking. A fitted t is more peaked as well as more heavy-tailed; its fitted scale is below the sample standard deviation, and at 5% the central concentration dominates. The t tail would overtake farther out.

regime.selection: Visual estimate of about 40 recent high-volatility days; a single-break Gaussian profile independently places the split one day later (39 recent observations).

conventions.historical_es: negative mean of all P&L observations at or below the historical VaR quantile; ties are included
conventions.historical_var: course RiskStats.jl rule: if m=n*alpha, negate the average of sorted P&L at one-based ranks floor(m) and ceil(m)
conventions.moments: mean, sample variance (n-1), bias-corrected skewness, and bias-corrected excess kurtosis
conventions.normal_var: -(sample mean P&L + Phi^{-1}(alpha) times sample P&L SD)
conventions.pnl: notional in dollars multiplied by one-year arithmetic return

prediction.basis: Each bond's >20% loss rate is below 5%, but the union rate is above 5%; the 5% quantile crosses a default-loss jump only after diversification. ES averages the worst tail, where the split position usually contains only one default.

conventions.central_day_definition: all three empirical rank uniforms strictly between 0.05 and 0.95

copula_parameter_counts.explanation: three pairwise correlations; t copula adds degrees of freedom

conventions.es_rule: negative mean P&L at or below the empirical quantile, including ties
conventions.simulation_variance_reduction: common correlated Normal draws for the two copulas
conventions.var_quantile_method: course RiskStats.jl: average the floor(n*alpha) and ceil(n*alpha) order statistics using one-based indices

conventions.expected_returns: zero as required: fitted alpha is reported but omitted from risk draws; market and residual simulations are centered at zero
conventions.ols: ordinary least squares with an intercept
conventions.random_numbers: full and diagonal residual models use common Gaussian draws
conventions.simulation_var: course RiskStats.jl rule: negate the average of sorted P&L at one-based ranks floor(n*0.05) and ceil(n*0.05)

prediction.basis: Positive residual covariance enters 2*w_A*w_B*cov(e_A,e_B): the term is positive for P1 and negative for P2.
